articleTitle: Optimum Power from Decentralized Sources in the Connecting Branches of Medium Voltage Distribution Networks
abstract: The paper describes the steps involved in short-term planning of medium voltage distribution networks. The optimum power from the decentralized energy sources in a connection branch for a selected short-term planning strategy is determined. Conclusions are drawn up regarding the minimum power losses in a long, heavily or lightly loaded branch, as well as in a short, heavily or lightly loaded one, both with connected decentralized energy sources.

articleTitle: Efficiency of the Neutral Grounding Mode in Medium Voltage Distribution Networks
abstract: The report presents a study of the efficiency of the different ways of grounding the neutral in traditional and smart medium voltage distribution networks. The magnitude of the efficiency indicator is determined for each of the neutral grounding modes for the following types of networks: a traditional grid, a smart grid with a connected decentralized energy source, and a smart grid with emergency connections to an adjacent branch. After comparing the obtained results, conclusions are drawn, which are useful for the operation of medium voltage distribution networks.

articleTitle: Opportunities for Energy Storage From Rooftop PV Plants for the Needs of Public Lighting in Municipalities
abstract: The report evaluated the use of rooftop hybrid photovoltaic power plant (PVPP) on municipal buildings for public lighting needs. The low cost of purchasing energy during the day makes it necessary to store it in solar rechargeable batteries (SRB) and use it at night. The selection of the size of the SRB is according to the annual power schedule for public lighting, with the necessary kWh for 1 kW of installed power determined for the adopted dimming mode of the luminaires.

articleTitle: Quantum Technology: Unleashing the Power and Shaping the Future of Cybersecurity
abstract: Cybersecurity refers to the practice of protecting computer systems, networks, and digital data from unauthorized access, attacks, damage, and theft. It involves implementing measures and techniques to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and computing resources. Cybersecurity encompasses various disciplines and activities to safeguard digital assets and prevent or mitigate potential threats [1]. Today, information security has emerged as one of the foremost challenges in our interconnected world. When we consider cyber security, the immediate concern that comes to mind is the exponential growth of cybercrimes. Governments and businesses alike are taking various measures to combat this form of criminal activity. Furthermore, there is a growing apprehension among individuals regarding cybersecurity issues. This paper primarily focuses on the concerns surrounding cyber security in relation to emerging technologies. It also delves into the advancements and ethical considerations that influence the field of cyber security [2]. Classical computers require significant time to solve these problems, making encryption secure. However, quantum computers have the potential to solve these problems much more efficiently than classical computers. However, the rapid progress in quantum computing technology necessitates proactive measures to develop and adopt quantum-resistant cryptographic solutions to ensure the long-term security of sensitive information. Ongoing research and collaboration between academia, industry, and standardization bodies are essential in addressing the quantum threat to cybersecurity [3].

articleTitle: Increasing the Efficiency of Lighting Objects in the Urban Environment
abstract: The work evaluates the effectiveness of internal lighting of buildings in the urban environment of Ukraine in accordance with the EN15193:2006 standard. The assessment was carried out based on the calculation of the value of the Lighting Energy Numeric Indicator followed by a parametric analysis of the factors that affect the value of this indicator. As an object of research, the lighting installations of internal lighting of buildings of social, cultural, and domestic purpose will be considered. The subject of research is the search for an effective value of the ratio of parameters, which consider the geometric dimensions and characteristics of the premises (length, width, height, wall paint, window sizes and degree of daylight penetration, working hours, type of light sources, number, and power of lamps, as well as the control method of them). A comparative assessment of various lighting installation options was carried out based on the calculation of the Lighting Energy Numeric Indicator lighting energy efficiency indicator for various combinations of parameters. Based on the results of the calculations, they were ranked and ways of improving the efficiency of the lighting installations of social, cultural, and domestic buildings were evaluated.

articleTitle: Cloud Service Module for Lighting Equipment Monitoring
abstract: Regulation 245/2009 is applied during the rehabilitation of public lighting in the European Community, with the primary requirement after the rehabilitation of the equipment being the monitoring of the “green” criteria set for lighting operation (EU GPPC RLTS). These criteria cover three main sections: energy consumption, light pollution (dimming of lighting after midnight), and overall operational costs of the equipment. This report describes a module used as an intermediary between the lighting management system and a web page, through which control authorities are able to monitor the compliance with the energy efficiency indicators set in the projects using standard devices (PC, tablet, phone).

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Photometric Characteristics and Efficacy of LED Luminaires for Indoor, Industrial and Street Lighting With and Without an Optical System
abstract: Measurement and analysis of photometric characteristics and efficacy of LED luminaires for indoor, industrial and street lighting with and without an optical system, are done in this paper. The results for the measured with a goniophotometer system, maximum luminous intensity, beam angle, field angle, total output luminous flux, luminaire efficacy, average luminance at vertical angular zones and light distribution for the different variants of the optical system of the tested LED luminaires are presented. The efficiency loss in the optical system elements of the tested LED luminaires is shown. Comparative lighting calculations of the tested indoor LED luminaire with and without reflector and grating anti-glare are done. Classification of the lateral and vertical light distribution according to the IES standard of the tested street LED luminaires with different variants of the optical system is done. Comparative optimal lighting calculations of both street LED luminaires without and with a secondary lens for road lighting designed according to the luminance requirement are done. Conclusions regarding the realized photometric indicators, glare, illuminance, and efficiency losses in optical system elements of the tested LED luminaires are done.

articleTitle: CLO for Stepwise Adaptive Lighting of Road Tunnels
abstract: When implementing adaptive lighting of road tunnels with non-dimmable illuminators, the main advantage of the new energy-efficient LED technologies - the CLO (constant light output) method - is lost. With it, by dimming the luminaires, an average of 15% of the energy for lighting is saved at 50,000 hours of resource of the luminaires. The report examines the possibility of implementing CLO with non-dimmable LED luminaires by currently changing the levels of L20 for controlling the group illuminators according to a 2006 patent of Technical University of Sofia.

articleTitle: Methods for Determining the Spectral Composition of LED Light Emission with the Use of Discrete Data from Spectroradiometers
abstract: The paper explores various methods for determining the spectral composition of the LED light sources emission by employing discrete readings obtained from spectroradiometers. Proposed is a novel approach to defining a mathematical model that accurately describes the spectral distribution of LEDs, by applying characteristic mathematical functions. Put forward, in this regard, is a clear definition for the use of “Envelop Function Model” (EFM). Suggested, furthermore, is an evaluation of the method's application in the analysis of typical LED light sources. The results obtained are then compared with those attained via the “Trapezoidal Rule” (TR) method, which serves as an integral characteristic of discrete functions. The methods, advanced in the paper, are considered quite appropriate for estimating the proportion of emission within a given wavelength range relative to the total emission in the visible spectrum. The method is equally applicable in assessing the compatibility of light sources that adhere to the standard EN 62471:2009 regarding the “Photo-biological safety of lamps and lamp system” [8], and in the provision of quantitative assessments of the emission proportions within specific wavelengths.

articleTitle: Design Concept for the Reconstruction of a Football Field Sports Lighting System in Accordance with Lighting Class III Specifications
abstract: Developed in the present paper is a concept for optimization of the luminaires used in the football fields for university, amateur, semiprofessional sports, etc. and their full-scale renovation in adherence to lighting class III specifications. Proposed is an effective method for achieving the lighting indicators outlined in the EN 12193 “Light and Lighting - Sport Lighting”. The study inludes a comparative analysis of lighting and energy parameters for the lighting system, as well as a techical-economic analysis to evaluate the feasibilty and profitability of the recommended technical solution. The conceptual approach discussed in the paper has already been implemented in the reconstruction of a real project - a stadium for university sporting events at the Tehnical University of Varna, Bulgaria.

articleTitle: Lymphocyte Phenotypes in Pheasants under Different Factors
abstract: For the phenotyping of lymphocytes we used spontaneous rosette tests and indirect rosette tests. Immunocytoadherent technic revealed that there is no difference in the absolute number of T- (E-ROK) according to the sex as well as the lymphocytes. Significantly higher values were detected in males compared to females B-lymphocytes We found that the number of B-lymphocytes (EAC-rossetes) and helper cells increases with age, and we showed the highest percentage of lymphocytes in autumn, which correlated with a higher percentage of T-helpers. The obtained data show not only the trends of the changes, but they are also the basis for analysis in various pathological conditions.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison and Analysis of AODV, DSDV and DSR Routing Protocols in VANET for Urban Scenario
abstract: In recent years, technology has developed very quickly. Telecommunications, artificial intelligence and computers are becoming a bigger part of our daily lives. Life without them is already unthinkable. Higher and higher data transmission speeds are being achieved. Thanks to this, systems such as ITS (Intelligent Transport Systems) are developed. The considered VANET (Vehicular ad hoc networks) network in this paper is also part of ITS. AODV (Ad hoc On-demand Distance Vector), DSDV (Destination Sequence Distance Vector) and DSR (Dynamic Source Routing) routing protocols are compared in an urban scenario. The construction of the connection route in this kind of network is very important because the reliability of the messages and the security of the connection depend on it.

articleTitle: Master Plan of Dupnitsa City
abstract: The Master Plan is plan for development of the city, of individual neighborhoods, localities and parks over the next 20–30 years. The master plan proposes a global concept that outlines the main directions and scope of future outdoor lighting. The ways and stages for its implementation are outlined. In the absence of a Master Plan, it is difficult to achieve coordination and harmonious lighting of individual neighboring sites

articleTitle: Investigation of the Color Shift of White Road Markings
abstract: The paper presents an investigation on the color characteristics – color coordinates (chromaticity) and luminance factor in daylight conditions of white road markings paint at different exploitation state. The chromaticity of new and exploited paints of the same kind have been measured along with their luminance factors and the color differences have been estimated. The results are presented in the CIE 1931 XYZ color space with the chromaticity regions of white marked in it.

Author Keywords: color shift of exploited road markings
chromaticity regions of white road markings

articleTitle: Hybrid Rooftop PV Plants and Determining the Size of Energy Storage Devices by Lighting Load
abstract: The construction of PV power plants (PVPP) on industrial buildings became necessary as an effective measure against the constantly changing supply price of electricity from the free market. Now, almost all the electricity produced on site by the PVPP is consumed by the enterprise, without entering into contracts for the sale of energy to the electricity distribution company (EDC). This approach simplifies the relationship with the EDC and allows for an equalization of the energy supply schedule from the free market. The report examines a case for selecting an energy storage facility from a PVPP based on a load schedule for the supply of energy from the free market before using the PVPP and a lighting load for premises with a two-shift mode of operation.

articleTitle: Review of Energy Management Systems for Small and Medium Enterprises
abstract: This article provides an overview of systems and methodologies used for energy management in small and medium-sized industrial enterprises. The main goal of the presented development is to examine basic principles in the management of energy flows in industrial enterprises powered by various renewable energy sources and energy storage elements. With the addition of additional energy sources, energy efficiency would significantly increase, which would also lead to a reduction in electricity costs.

articleTitle: Thermal Effect of Solar Irradiance on Decorative Tube-Shaped LED Lamps
abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to show that under the thermal effect of solar irradiance, the temperature of decorative tube-shaped light-emitting diode (LED) lamps can rise to values that can permanently destroy the lamps or cause a fire, regardless of whether the lamps are operating or not. The light diffuser of the considered LED lamp is made of two polycarbonate cylinders nested in each other. The considered problem is modeled analytically in MATLAB and numerically in COMSOL, and the data obtained analytically are used as inputs for the numerical model. The analytical model is based on empirical correlations for heat transfer, while the numerical model is based on the finite element method (FEM). Images taken by a thermal imaging camera are used as an experimental background. It is found that the outer hollow cylinder of the light diffuser behaves like a cylindrical solar concentrator, which in steady-state can raise the temperature of the inner solid cylinder of the light diffuser up to 218.2 °C.

articleTitle: Security Threats and Models in the Field of Renewable Energy Systems
abstract: Electricity is a crucial part of everyday life, being used in almost every aspect and any field of work. Nowadays renewable energy systems are being built, because of their sustainable way of producing electricity, and making the world safer and cleaner. With their integration and use in households and even countries' whole infrastructures, their outage and disruption of the production process can cause serious issues. Energy systems are directly connected to the economic situation of a country and a single failure can create a cascade of disturbances. Because of the digitalization and requirements for remote monitoring of the equipment used in such systems, they have become more vulnerable and can be exploited by malicious intruders over the Internet. In this research we will examine the different types of cyber threats concerning the security of renewable energy systems. We will introduce a defense strategy model to secure the infrastructure of a renewable energy system.

articleTitle: Back-Up LED Lighting System with a Bidirectional SEPIC-ZETA Converter Based – A Computer Study
abstract: In the present work, a back-up power supply system for LED lighting, including a DC voltage source, a bidirectional SEPIC-ZETA converter, an ultracapacitor and a control system is considered. The study was carried out by means of a computer simulation, showing operating time diagrams in the different modes. The operation of the control system and the functions of the regulators included in it are described.

articleTitle: Copy Services: A Client's Shield Against Data Loss
abstract: This article will discuss the importance of copy services in securing data and ensuring business continuity, specifically IBM Copy Services. We will highlight the primary reasons why clients prefer IBM Copy Services, including data protection, disaster recovery, high availability, backup and restore data. We will also differentiate between Disaster Recovery (DR) and Business Continuity (BC), with DR focused on restoring IT systems and data while BC ensures the continuity of all business operations. Additionally, we will explain concepts such as “Recovery Time Objective (RTO)” and “Recovery Point Objective” (RPO), emphasizing their significance in business continuity planning. Finally, we will emphasize the critical role played by IBM's Copy Services in safeguarding against data loss and ensuring business continuity in today's volatile digital age.

articleTitle: Detailed Check-Up of Trees Using Modern Technologies
abstract: This article is pointing some differences in maintaining trees between Bulgaria and Germany. Starting from the visual assessment the trees are supposed to be regularly checked, after facing difficult cases detailed check-up is supposed to be performed using modern technologies. Which will lead to the proper execution of the pruning.

articleTitle: A Case Study on Compensating Reactive Power of Medium Voltage Cables
abstract: A case study on reactive power compensation of an industrial building with additional compensation devices is presented in this paper. Control of reactive power in industrial environment is of significant importance as it can cause active power losses, deformation of triangle of powers, voltage losses and reduce electrical energy's quality. Furthermore, reactive power, outside of norms, is heavily fined. Thus, the purpose of the case study is to reduce billings' costs caused by excess reactive power outside of norms. Due to loads being non-linear and due to the changes in their signs, reactive power is compensated by installing compensation devices (capacitor banks and shunt reactors) on low-voltage sections in a step control manner. Based on obtained results, reactive power compensation can be performed easily and billings' costs can be reduced.

articleTitle: A Virtual Light Laboratory - Application For Students Training
abstract: The report presents the application of a developed virtual light laboratory for training lighting students. Some of the application possibilities of the developed software product are shown. Moments from working with the product are presented. Product capabilities are summarized. Some advantages and disadvantages compared to existing similar products are outlined. Shown are screenshots of the product's performance and data that can be obtained and a summary. The relevant conclusions are drawn.

articleTitle: Unveiling IBM's Strategy for Advanced Copy Services Replications
abstract: This article provides an overview of IBM's Copy Services available for the “DS8000” Data Storage Enterprise Devices series. The “DS8000” series offers a range of Copy Services, which can be managed using the IBM System Storage. A notable feature is the point-in-time copy function, “FlashCopy”, which allows for the creation of volume data copies in storage systems. The primary functions of Copy Services encompass”disaster recovery”, data migration, and data duplication solutions. The article further delves into various replication techniques, such as “Metro Mirror”, Global Copy, and”Global Mirror”, and introduces advanced features like “Safeguarded Copy”, which offers protection against logical data corruption.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of Mononuclear Cells of Different Origin to Fumonisin $\mathrm{B}_{1}$
abstract: If in the years of the last century the consumption of fruits and vegetables was considered a prerequisite for longevity, today this thesis is being questioned. And the reason is primarily natural pollutants, to which mycotoxins belong. High humidity and elevated average annual temperatures, improper conditions during transport and storage, are a favorable prerequisite for fungal contamination and an increase in the levels of synthesized mycotoxins. According to data from the International Agency for Research on Cancer, fusariotoxins, together with aflatoxins, belong to the group of carcinogenic substances of particular importance to farm animals and humans. The aim of the present communication is to follow the cytotoxic activity of fumonisin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{B}_{\mathbf{1}}$</tex> on mononuclear cells of different origins (human lymphocytes from different blood groups, lymphocytes derived from large ruminants and from pigs). In order to establish the cytotoxic effect of the mycotoxin fumonisin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{B}_{\mathbf{1}}$</tex> on mononuclear cells, we used different concentrations (15, 40 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{100}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{g}/\mathbf{ml}$</tex>) and different durations of incubation - 12, 24 and 48 hours. Studies have shown cytotoxic activity of fumonisin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{B}_{\mathbf{1}}$</tex> towards mononuclear cells, which is dose and time dependent. The highest stability was demonstrated in bovine lymphocytes and in human blood group zero. The results supported the hypothesis that mycotoxins are a serious health problem for humans and animals and a factor in immunosuppression.

articleTitle: Internet Monitoring of Lighting Systems Using the Power Grid as a Communication Medium
abstract: The paper presents lighting control systems for street, sport, industrial and tunnel lighting systems, developed in the Technical University of Sofia, that use the power grid as a communication medium. Their upgrade with a cloud service for remote control ensures their monitoring from any device with access to the Internet (PC, tablet, phone).

articleTitle: A Study on the Operation of Own Needs' Equipment Under Fault Conditions
abstract: A study on the operating regimes of own needs' power equipment under fault conditions has been performed. The purpose of the study is to investigate the operation of own needs' power equipment on medium voltage 6 kV (motors and transformers) under fault conditions. The following fault conditions are studied - single-phase open circuit, double-phase open circuit and single-phase open circuit with earth fault. Based on obtained results only own needs' transformers (6/0.4 kV) operate with asymmetrical currents which values do not exceed their respective protection thresholds. With regards to own needs' motors there is always at least one current value that exceeds set protection threshold.

articleTitle: Modelling of Own Needs' Equipment During Faults
abstract: The behaviour of a power station's own needs' power equipment during open circuit fault conditions is modelled and presented in this paper. The considered situation is with reduced loads on own needs' sections. Based on obtained results it can be concluded that albeit the caused significant imbalances, there is always at least one faulty phase current of own needs' power equipment that trips protection accordingly.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Variables Determining the Amount of Stray Currents in Electrified Urban Surface Transport in Sofia
abstract: Electrified urban rail transport is an important part of the infrastructure of every European city. Along with the benefits it provides, electrified rail transport can be a serious source of stray currents, which have a negative impact on a city's underground infrastructure. This report presents measurements made in five rail sections in the city of Bavaria. Sofia of parameters that determine the magnitude of stray currents due to electrified rail transport.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Measures for Improving the Energy Efficiency of Medium-Sized Enterprises
abstract: In the presented article, an assessment and measurements were realized to determine the energy efficiency of a medium-sized industrial enterprise. Real data from a three-shift plant was used. An assessment of the current electricity consumption was made and an energy audit was carried out to reduce electricity costs. The main goal of the current research is to ensure the basic functionality of the buildings, as well as the production-technological process, ensuring minimum electricity costs and maximum efficiency.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Life Expectancy Prediction for IGBT with Neural Network and Noise Data
abstract: This paper presents a study focused on utilizing neural networks (NN) to forecast the lifespan of electronic components. These components are susceptible to deterioration over time caused by aging, environmental factors, and other issues. Accurately predicting the remaining useful life of these components is crucial for enhancing reliability and minimizing downtime. Earlier, we introduce a neural network-based approach to estimate the life expectancy of electronic components with correct data. This study presents a logical extension, where the same NN is try against “noisy” data. Moreover, by simulating real-world variations and uncertainties, the model becomes more adaptable and capable of handling unforeseen circumstances in electronic component lifespan prediction. This noise-aided training approach ensures that the neural network is not overly reliant on ideal or noise-free data, making it more reliable and resilient in practical applications.

articleTitle: Indoor LED Luminaire Reflector Profile Optimization to Minimize the RUG Glare Index
abstract: The paper presents a methodology for optimizing an optical system, in terms of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{UG}$</tex> glare index, by iterative change of the reflector shape of an indoor LED luminaire with rotational symmetry of the light distribution intended for indoor workplaces. Building of 3D models of an optical system of indoor LED luminaire by iterative changing of the reflector shape by using software for optical design and photometric analysis was made. Comparative photometric analysis using the Monte Carlo raytracing method of the modelled optical systems with an iterative change of the reflector shape of the LED luminaire to calculate their photometric characteristics was done. Comparative lighting calculations with an optimum criterion – minimizing of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{R}_{\boldsymbol{UG}}\leq \mathbf{19}$</tex>, meeting the requirements of lighting standard for a typical office room, through the analysis of which the optimal solution is found.

articleTitle: Biodynamic Lighting Systems and Influence of the Correlated Color Temperature over the Educational Working Process
abstract: The paper presents a test method investigation of the students' ability for effective participation in the educational process depending on the controlled illuminance level and correlated color temperature. The practical results refer to different age groups and workplaces. The discomfort perception in the varying lighting situations is evaluated as well.

articleTitle: Energy Management
abstract: The importance of energy management and a sustainable energy production, supply, consumption and implementation became more crucial than ever it was, due to declining of fossil energy resources, environmental pollution, energy demand, energy prices and last but not the least which is climate change. Therefore, energy management and renewable energy management is a key tool which could play an important role in consumption and efficient usage of energy sources specially in developing countries, tropic and subtropics via a holistic renewable energy concept and energy management systems, while in modern countries it will help to decrease the usage of fossils for energy production, reduction in prices, energy saving, reduction in demand of both production and supply.

articleTitle: Daily Adaptive Lighting for Swimming Pools
abstract: Sports lighting energy demand is a significant part of the maintenance expenses for all kind of indoor halls. The daylight adaptation of the lighting design gives opportunities for significant reduction of the consumed energy per year. The paper presents a daily adaptive solution for the lighting design of the indoor swimming pool in the Sport's Department of the Technical University of Sofia.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Non Image Forming Effects of Existing Human Centric Lighting Systems
abstract: The paper presents an investigation of the potential for stimulation of the retinal photoreceptors and emergence of non-image forming effects of two different existing human centric lighting systems in an educational building. The radiant fluxes and the spectral power distributions of the letter are measured at different correlated color temperatures and the non-visual potentials of the lighting systems are estimated by means of CIE S 26 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex>-opic methodology.

Author Keywords: non image forming effects of light

articleTitle: Artistic Architectural Lighting of the Historical Museum in Kardzhali
abstract: An artistic concept was created for the lighting of the historical museum in the city of Kardzhali: A day and night inspection of the site was carried out. Based on the cadastral plan and site inspections, an assessment was made according to “A Guide to Urban Lighting Master planning - CIE 234:2019”. The reflection coefficients of the facade were measured and realistic textures were created. Visualization of the museum's artistic-architectural lighting concept was completed using a computer modeling and visualization software program that creates a beautifully realistic picture of the future exterior.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of the Blue Light Hazard Efficacy of Luminous Radiation of Indoor LED Lamps
abstract: Measurement and analysis of the blue light hazard efficacy of luminous radiation of different indoor LED lamps are done in this paper. Measurements of spectral power distribution, photometric, colourimetric parameters and efficacy of 21 tested indoor LED lamps with a CCD spectroradiometer in an integrating sphere in tabular form are presented. Comparison of the spectral dependences of blue light hazard weighting function, measured spectral power distribution and Blue Weighted Watts of the indoor LED lamps studied, having different correlated colour temperature is done. Graphical and defined linear analytical dependence of blue light hazard efficacy of luminous radiation on the correlated colour temperature of the measured indoor LED lamps are done. Conclusions regarding the measured and calculated blue light hazard level control indicators of the tested indoor LED lamps are made.

articleTitle: Cellular and Humoral Defense Mechanisms of the Mammary Gland in Sheep with Subclinical Mastitis
abstract: Subclinical mastitis is a mammary gland disease with a high prevalence and complex diagnostics. Innate and adaptive immunity are the main protective factors of the organ. The aim of this study was to determine the changes in some specific and non-specific defence factors of the mammary gland. The results showed that the main cell population in milk obtained from healthy animals was macrophages (51%), and in the presence of subclinical mastitis PMNs (68.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) whit increase of their oxygen-dependent microbicidal activity. Lysozyme and lactoferrin levels also rise (by 198% and 337<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) in affected animals. Measurements of immunoglobulin levels showed elevations in IgG (by 41<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), IgM (by 79<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and IgA (by 75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). The development of subclinical mastitis in sheep leads to an increase in PMNs and their microbicidal activity in milk. In the presence of subclinical mastitis, the levels of lysozyme and lactoferrin, as well as the concentrations of immunoglobulins IgG, IgM and IgA elevates.

articleTitle: Understanding lighting users' preferences through a real experience approach using mixed methods
abstract: At present, most lighting systems operate following standards that do not adjust to the preferences and needs of the users, far less to the multiple changing tasks that they can develop. For a system to properly adapt to the needs and preferences of the users it would first be necessary to know: what do these users prefer and need? To answer this question, this paper proposes an experiment using qualitative data supported with quantitative data. This experiment is made up of 17 experiences in which on each occasion a different participant is working for 1 hour with 3 different lighting settings (neutral, cool, and warm) that change automatically. During this hour, in addition to their normal work with a computer or tablet, the participants must carry out various activities on paper. These participants can modify both the flux and the Correlated Colour Temperature (CCT) of the lighting throughout the experience. At the end of each experience, users also participate individually in a semi-structured interview. The results of the analysis show that users are not comfortable with the standard settings and that they prefer to decide on the lighting settings themselves, either by creating profiles or modifying them manually. This work mostly concludes that for a lighting system to be able to adapt to the preferences and needs of the users, these systems must be flexible, allowing the users themselves to make the changes and adapt the lighting to their needs.
